name: A* Algorithm
description: Combines Dijkstra's guaranteed-shortest-path with a heuristic that guides search toward the goal. Uses f(n)=g(n)+h(n) to prioritize nodes closest to the goal, skipping irrelevant directions.
aim: Find the shortest path from start to goal using f(n)=g(n)+h(n), where g(n) is the actual cost from start and h(n) is a heuristic estimate of the remaining cost. Much faster than Dijkstra's for point-to-point pathfinding.
howItWorks: Initialize open set with start node; f(start)=h(start)
Pick node with lowest f score from open set
If it's the goal — reconstruct and return path
For each neighbor: compute g(neighbor) = g(current) + cost
Update if better path found; add to open set
The heuristic h(n) must be admissible (never overestimates)

complexity.spaceDescription: Open/closed sets hold at most O(V) nodes

realWorld: Google Maps and GPS: fastest route planning on road networks
Video games: NPC pathfinding in games like StarCraft, Minecraft
Robotics: autonomous navigation and motion planning
whenToUse: When a good distance heuristic is available
Faster than Dijkstra's when goal is known
alternatives: Dijkstra's Algorithm: guaranteed shortest path, no heuristic needed (slower)

beginnerAnalogy: Like a GPS that not only knows the distance driven so far, but also makes a smart guess about how far the destination still is — so it focuses on roads leading toward the destination instead of exploring in all directions.
beginnerWhat: A smarter version of Dijkstra's that uses a 'hint' about how close the goal is to explore fewer dead ends.
beginnerWhy: The heuristic hint dramatically reduces the number of nodes explored compared to Dijkstra's.
beginnerWhen: When you need fastest path between two specific points and have a distance estimate (GPS, grid navigation, games).
